service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment in Vail
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats, incentive events and private celebrations at Vail venues, solo through quartet.

faqs.q: How does load-in work at a Vail hotel?
faqs.a: Through the dock, on a scheduled window. Vail Village and Lionshead keep cars out of their cores, so hotels receive vendors at loading docks and move gear by freight elevator. We settle dock time, the elevator window and the route to the floor with the venue in writing before the day.

faqs.q: Does the altitude change the performance?
faqs.a: It changes the plan more than the sound. At 8,150 feet singers and horns pace differently, instruments drift with the wider temperature swing between sound check and the last set, and we plan a longer sound check. The fee for the music doesn't change.

faqs.q: What does travel to Vail cost?
faqs.a: Travel is its own line on the quote, covering the I-70 drive from Denver and the hours around it. A late curfew can add a night's lodging, which is on the quote before you sign.

faqs.q: Can part of the evening run outdoors?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it. Vail's outdoor cap in the resort villages was reported at 65 dBA, measured ten feet from the permitted area, and the town was reviewing its rules when we checked, so we confirm the current figure with your venue.

faqs.q: Which venues host retreat evenings in Vail?
faqs.a: Most of the calendar runs through the village hotels: the Sonnenalp, Four Seasons Resort Vail, The Arrabelle at Vail Square, Grand Hyatt Vail and The Hythe, with Donovan Pavilion as the town's own event venue. Each has its own dock schedule, cap and curfew, and the plan is built against all three.
